To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the basolateral ATP effect is mediated by a P2X(3) receptor, which is composed of P2X(2) and P2X4 subunits.
basolateral P(2)X(4) receptors are responsible for inhibition of Na(2) absorption in the mouse medullary TAL.
the nonselective cations channel P2X(3) is involved in the inhibition of NaCl absorption in the mTAL.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of extracellular nucleotides in the regulation of renal epithelia and their transport functions.
the identification of the molecular mechanisms that underlie the inhibition of NaCl absorption by basolateral ATP.
the molecular mechanisms of P2 receptor function in the kidney.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ATP inhibits NaCl absorption in mouse m-TAL via basolateral P(2X(4)) receptor.
basolateral P(2X) receptors mediate inhibition by ATP in mouse mTAl.
basolateral P(2)X(4) and P(2)Y(2) receptor subtypes are present in mouse mTal and mediate inhibition of solute reabsorption.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ATP inhibits NaCl absorption in mouse mAL via luminal P2Y(4) and basolateral, P2X(2), P2X4, and P2X1 receptors.
ATP inhibits transport in mTAL via luminal and, in addition, basolateral P(2) receptors.
luminal ATP inhibits NaCl transport in mTAL via luminal P2Y(1/2/4) and P2X receptors, whereas basolateral ATP inhibits Na(+) absorption via P2X(2/4/5/7) and P2Y(4) receptors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
P2X4 receptors are involved in the ATP-induced transport inhibition in mouse mTAl.
P2X receptors can inhibit epithelial NaCl transport.
P2X(2) receptors are expressed in mouse medullar thick ascending limbs and that they mediate inhibition of sodium transport in mouse medulla.
